curation: Analyst-reviewed distinct cause/effect groups; variants and uncertain propagation are explicit. This catalog is selective, not exhaustive.

scenarios.title: Encrypted RTSP request fails ticket authentication
scenarios.scope: connection rejection; authenticated ticket cleanup is conditional
scenarios.trigger: No matching peer ticket verifies the encrypted envelope.
scenarios.behavior: Tickets::authenticate returns request_authentication_failed. Legacy Connection::read returns Step::Close; the typed policy version reports Step::Failure to the common handler, whose permit authorizes Transport::close. An unauthenticated connection does not identify an active stream ticket.
scenarios.reason: Authorization and authenticated sequence state must remain protected; an invalid connection is not proof that a legitimate active stream failed.
scenarios.next_action: Route the original authentication failure to the final network decision boundary while retaining fail-closed verification and ticket-scoped effects.

scenarios.title: A ticket ID or encryption key is reused
scenarios.scope: prepared-ticket admission rejection
scenarios.trigger: Tickets::add sees a previously used ID or key.
scenarios.behavior: Ticket admission returns an explicit error before inserting the new ticket. Caller handling remains visible as candidate paths in the raw evidence.
scenarios.reason: Reuse protection participates in identity/crypto safety; do not discard its retained history to make startup succeed.
scenarios.next_action: Preserve the refusal and trace the authenticated launch reply through the owner; centralize the decision without reusing nonce/identity state.

scenarios.title: Active prepared-ticket capacity is exhausted
scenarios.scope: new ticket/startup refusal; existing streams may continue
scenarios.trigger: The active ticket count reaches MAX_TICKETS.
scenarios.behavior: Tickets::add returns ticket_limit. It does not itself remove an existing ticket.
scenarios.reason: A bounded-capacity refusal can be transient; this does not justify terminating existing streams or ignoring the bound.
scenarios.next_action: Confirm caller retry behavior and report a request-scoped capacity refusal centrally; retain the existing capacity cap.

scenarios.title: Retained ticket identity history is exhausted
scenarios.scope: new-ticket admission refusal
scenarios.trigger: The anti-reuse history reaches MAX_TICKET_HISTORY.
scenarios.behavior: Ticket admission returns ticket_history_limit rather than recycling retained identifiers.
scenarios.reason: This limit protects history used for reuse checks; treating it like an expendable diagnostic cache is unsafe without a proven new epoch policy.
scenarios.next_action: Keep the fence; review safe epoch/retirement and owner recovery before changing admission.

scenarios.title: RTSP pending-request backlog is full
scenarios.scope: one RTSP request receives 503
scenarios.trigger: The controller is busy and pending_network has reached MAX_PENDING_NETWORK.
scenarios.behavior: In the populated-main and ed2 reference sources, poll_transport replies 503 directly. The newer policy working source uses a request budget/backpressure instead; absence of the old refusal anchor is reported per snapshot and is not an active bypass finding.
scenarios.reason: Queue saturation needs a request-level decision and retry contract; it is not proof that the active stream must end.
scenarios.next_action: For a version that still refuses here, centralize the final decision while retaining bounded storage and existing tickets. For the newer budget path, test backpressure and connection deadlines separately.

scenarios.title: Shutdown/quiescence refuses a new PLAY
scenarios.scope: new start refusal while prepared ownership is retained
scenarios.trigger: A Ready record receives PLAY after shutdown_deadline was announced.
scenarios.behavior: handle_network sends 503, reinserts the record and returns before the common handler.
scenarios.reason: The host must stop admitting native starts during quiescence; whether the client can retry is distinct from resource retirement.
scenarios.next_action: Centralize this admission decision while retaining DAG-ordered quiescence and prepared ownership until normal cleanup.

scenarios.title: Negotiation sequence/pending/state refusal preserves the stream
scenarios.scope: request rejection with stream retained in policy-owner snapshot
scenarios.trigger: Negotiation rejects InvalidSequence, WrongState or Pending without changing negotiation state.
scenarios.behavior: The populated-main snapshot closes on every negotiation error. In policy snapshots with the reviewed Error::is_critical predicate, the three unchanged-state variants are noncritical and the common handler retains the stream while refusing the request. Evidence is labeled by source snapshot.
scenarios.reason: The owner regression work establishes unchanged negotiation state and retry behavior for these variants; it does not allow malformed security/media input.
scenarios.next_action: Integrate and qualify the owner fix once; exercise an invalid request followed by a valid retry and verify the ticket remains live.

scenarios.title: A controller record is not Ready or Playing
scenarios.scope: request-only RTSP 455
scenarios.trigger: An existing record is in another state before negotiation is called.
scenarios.behavior: The controller sends 455, reinserts the record and returns. This is a separate early branch from Negotiation::WrongState.
scenarios.reason: The state may represent preparation or cleanup. A request refusal is not automatically a recoverable stream condition.
scenarios.next_action: Keep the state/ownership guard, establish allowed client retry states, and route the final response through the common decision boundary.

scenarios.title: A prepared ticket expires before PLAY
scenarios.scope: RTSP 454 plus ticket closure/revocation
scenarios.trigger: A Ready record reaches its preparation expiry.
scenarios.behavior: The same guarded branch sends 454, closes the record with prepare_expired and revokes the ticket. These observations form one expiry scenario.
scenarios.reason: Expired admission/ownership must not be silently extended; resource cleanup remains required.
scenarios.next_action: Centralize the expiry decision and test exact ticket retirement; do not bypass the expiry fence to accept late PLAY.

scenarios.title: A network request has no controller ticket record
scenarios.scope: RTSP 454 request refusal
scenarios.trigger: records.remove(ticket) returns None.
scenarios.behavior: The let-else branch sends 454 and returns without creating a replacement record.
scenarios.reason: The request has no established owner state. Accepting it would bypass admission identity.
scenarios.next_action: Preserve refusal; pass the missing-owner condition to the final handler without fabricating ownership.

scenarios.title: An authenticated connection disappears during work
scenarios.scope: ticket closure with pending-operation settlement
scenarios.trigger: Disconnected has a known ticket and the reason is not response_complete.
variants: pending native mutation versus already-playing media
scenarios.behavior: disconnected cancels retained broker work, closes the record and revokes the ticket. The policy owner still has this separate terminal path.
scenarios.reason: An authenticated RTSP transaction can end while media still runs. A one-request TCP socket/timeout is not automatically loss of the required media/control transport; uncertain native mutation still requires settlement and retirement proof.
scenarios.next_action: Trace the connection fault origin, record state and pending operation. Distinguish an aborted request from required transport loss before letting the final handler terminate the stream; preserve exact operation identity and retirement fences.

scenarios.title: A selected audio contract cannot be opened
scenarios.scope: stream startup failure path
scenarios.trigger: An enabled/selected audio resource returns an incompatible negotiated format.
scenarios.behavior: opened returns an explicit error for the selected audio/processing contract; its caller routes an opened error to Job::fail.
scenarios.reason: A selected required format may not be replaced or disabled without an explicit fallback contract.
scenarios.next_action: Verify stream_audio and required-resource guards, preserve the selected contract, and trace the precise failure report to the central owner.

scenarios.title: Required video startup reports failure
scenarios.scope: stream startup failure path
scenarios.trigger: A video readiness response reports startup failure.
scenarios.behavior: The consume readiness closure returns video_startup_failed; its terminal propagation must be checked separately from the error-origin evidence.
scenarios.reason: Video is required for this stream contract; an unverified provider result cannot establish a running stream.
scenarios.next_action: Test the startup response and timeout at the selected provider boundary and preserve central handling of required-video failure.

scenarios.title: Lifecycle ownership journal cannot be persisted
scenarios.scope: startup/cleanup failure with ownership fence
scenarios.trigger: The journal write or its validated response fails.
scenarios.behavior: The journal failure path invokes Job::fail; this leads to a concrete stopping state through the stream-session workflow sink.
scenarios.reason: Durable ownership cannot be inferred after an unsuccessful write; warning-only treatment could permit unsafe reuse.
scenarios.next_action: Retain the ownership fence and exact cleanup identity; make the handler decide from the original storage failure rather than a generic lower-layer severity guess.

scenarios.title: The active capture binding is invalid
scenarios.scope: required capture/startup or active-session failure
scenarios.trigger: The lifecycle capture-binding validation branch fails.
scenarios.behavior: consume sends the concrete capture binding failure to Job::fail.
scenarios.reason: Capture authorization/identity is required; keep the original invalidation reason and ownership proof.
scenarios.next_action: Confirm the failing binding generation and route its report centrally; do not substitute an unrelated display/capture source.

scenarios.title: Capture observation cannot establish the selected source
scenarios.scope: required-source admission failure
scenarios.trigger: The required lifecycle capture observation is unavailable.
scenarios.behavior: consume invokes Job::fail for the required observation branch.
scenarios.reason: No observation does not establish authorized source ownership; a read failure and successful native retirement are different facts.
scenarios.next_action: Review bounded retry versus real denial, retaining required capture authorization before allowing startup.

scenarios.title: Optional stream maintenance is unavailable
scenarios.scope: active stream continues with bounded fallback in owner snapshot
scenarios.trigger: A nonallocating maintenance operation times out, is absent, refuses, or returns malformed optional data.
scenarios.behavior: The owner maintenance path skips or backs off, settles bookkeeping independently, emits a demoted report and calls the common handler. Security/recovery exceptions are a separate scenario.
scenarios.reason: These operations have explicit compatible fallbacks in this snapshot; the four operation variants are listed, not counted as four copies of every Err/cancel/report observation.
scenarios.next_action: Qualify the four operation fallbacks and their bounded settlement queue; retain original permission and ownership exceptions.

scenarios.title: Maintenance reports a real permission or recovery failure
scenarios.scope: active stream may stop through central critical gate
scenarios.trigger: The maintenance result explicitly requires cleanup/recovery, or a protected operation returns permission_denied.
scenarios.behavior: The owner uses StreamFailure::critical and Job::fail for these exceptions instead of the ordinary skip path.
scenarios.reason: Optional scheduling does not make authorization and unresolved native ownership optional.
scenarios.next_action: Keep exception tests separate from availability/fallback tests; preserve central critical handling and exact retirement proof.

scenarios.title: History release fails after the media decision
scenarios.scope: background retry; application/stream decision is retained
scenarios.trigger: A history-only release is rejected or unconfirmed.
scenarios.behavior: demote_history_release reports a bounded demotion, retains a background retry identity and removes history as an admission blocker.
scenarios.reason: This is a diagnostic/history operation, provided actual RTSP/application/native retirement remains independently fenced.
scenarios.next_action: Verify exact activity ID, bounded retry and non-history cleanup proof; do not treat this fallback as evidence of native retirement.

scenarios.title: Frame-limiter planning has no usable optional backend
scenarios.scope: no-op plan with warning in populated provider snapshot
scenarios.trigger: The read-only optional frame-limiter planning path cannot provide a backend.
scenarios.behavior: demote_to_no_op constructs a demoted issue with noop_frame_limiter. The provider is unavailable as a symlink in the policy-owner worktree.
scenarios.reason: The permitted fallback is planning-only and does not establish retirement of a previously applied native effect.
scenarios.next_action: Review the planning-only caller guard and retain mutation/recovery failures as critical.

scenarios.title: Display snapshot or verification fails on resume
scenarios.scope: resume refusal versus startup cleanup depends on retained state
scenarios.trigger: The required display snapshot is unavailable before resuming.
scenarios.behavior: The call goes through fail_before_resume_stream, which chooses reject_resume for the retained-session case and fail_record otherwise.
scenarios.reason: A failed resume and an instruction to destroy a retained application are different effects; the helper contains that distinction.
scenarios.next_action: Test both retained-session and initial-start branches. Centralize the original display condition without collapsing them into one terminal action.

scenarios.title: An input authorization lease has expired
scenarios.scope: input renewal rejection; whole-stream effect needs caller review
scenarios.trigger: The input renewal response has expired relative to now.
scenarios.behavior: accept_input_renewal returns input_lease_expired. A static caller chain alone does not prove whole-stream termination.
scenarios.reason: Do not silently extend input authorization or infer a view-only fallback that was not requested.
scenarios.next_action: Follow renewal failure through the central owner and test any explicitly configured view-only fallback separately.

scenarios.title: Processing-provider composition is invalid
scenarios.scope: provider startup propagation; stream impact unconfirmed
scenarios.trigger: A selected processing composition fails its contract validation.
scenarios.behavior: The raw candidate chain reaches this error from Video::start through the SDK composition validator. It is not proof of the final wire rejection.
scenarios.reason: Required contract identity and allocation ownership must not be bypassed to admit an invalid provider composition.
scenarios.next_action: Confirm whether the host catches or escalates this ModuleResult, then connect the exact stream decision across the module boundary.

scenarios.title: The client explicitly tears down the stream
scenarios.scope: authorized stop, excluded from failure counts
scenarios.trigger: A valid negotiation action requests Teardown.
scenarios.behavior: The controller closes with no failure reason and schedules Stop. This must not be counted as a critical startup error.
scenarios.reason: Normal requested shutdown has separate authorization and retirement requirements.
scenarios.next_action: Keep it outside the failure triage queue and verify ordinary retirement without inventing a failure classification.

scenarios.title: The requested streaming mode is explicitly disabled
scenarios.scope: new stream admission refusal
scenarios.trigger: The selected mode has no enabled stream configuration.
scenarios.behavior: The distinct branches both call fail_record with streaming_disabled, which forwards the failure to Record::request_cleanup. They are one policy cause with two branch variants, not two copies of every cleanup observation.
scenarios.reason: An explicit disabling policy must be honored; it is not an optional diagnostic failure.
scenarios.next_action: Keep admission disabled, report the exact disabled mode to the final handler and preserve retained-session cleanup semantics.

scenarios.title: ANNOUNCE does not match the accepted media/profile contract
scenarios.scope: ANNOUNCE refusal and conditional ticket closure
scenarios.trigger: The media/profile acceptance predicate reports failure: legacy success=false completion, or a typed Err outcome at finish_network_result.
variants: required contract versus compatible lower bitrate
scenarios.behavior: The legacy helper maps an acceptance boolean to unsuccessful completion/closure. The typed policy version carries Result<NetworkCompletion, StreamFailure> into finish_network_result; the common decision selects critical rejection/closure or operation-scoped refusal. A mismatch label alone still does not identify the failing field.
scenarios.reason: An error label alone cannot distinguish an invalid selected format/encryption contract from a compatible lower bitrate. The acceptance predicate and requested/effective values require review.
scenarios.next_action: Trace each rejecting field predicate through Config::negotiate_announce; test a compatible lower bitrate separately from codec, geometry, encryption and transport violations. Do not classify every mismatch as critical or disable security checks.
